name: Prize crossword No 25,472
preamble: All the pieces are of a kind from the same hand

clue.text: Expert to dump moth

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast who knows a subject well
to tip rubbish is to dump it

explanation.surface: An instruction to an expert to get rid of a moth that has been bothering someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert' reads as an adjective or a person consulted, but it is just a synonym; the definition sits quietly at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The buff-tip is a common European moth whose folded wings resemble a broken birch twig.

clue.text: Composer is god if he changes ends

indicators.note: trading ends means one final letter is swapped out for another word's final letter
an end is the last letter, so only the closing letter of the other word is kept

blocks.note: Brahma is the Hindu creator god; its final A is dropped
the last letter of 'is' takes the place of the god's last letter

explanation.surface: A remark that a composer counts as divine provided he alters his endings.
explanation.walkthrough: The god and the little word 'is' swap their last letters, so the god's closing A gives way to S.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was the German Romantic composer of four symphonies and the German Requiem.

clue.text: Piece working for KLM?

blocks.note: surface reading: an item or article, here one of the theme's operas by the same composer
setter's reading: KLM is the Dutch national airline, so a man employed there who takes to the air is an airborne Netherlander

explanation.surface: A query about some item or employee at the Dutch airline.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says every 'piece' is an opera by the same hand, here Wagner; KLM is Royal Dutch Airlines, so its aircrew are literally Dutchmen in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Der fliegende Holländer is Wagner's opera about a ghostly sea captain doomed to sail forever.

clue.text: Property in Berlin retained by 6d piece

indicators.note: what is retained is kept and held inside something else

blocks.note: a tanner was the old British sixpenny coin, written 6d before decimalisation
Haus is the German word for a house

explanation.surface: A German house held on to by someone with a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: '6d' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down, but it is the old British sixpence, nicknamed a tanner. The preamble supplies the definition: another Wagner opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannhäuser is Wagner's opera about a minstrel knight torn between sacred and profane love, so it is one of the preamble's pieces.

clue.text: City coppers in Scotland

blocks.note: first meaning: a Greek city-state
second meaning: the Scots word for police officers

explanation.surface: Urban police officers north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers are police officers; in Scots the police are 'the polis'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for a city-state is used in English, and Scots pronounce and spell police that way too.

clue.text: Fight with the Queen's violinist?

blocks.note: a scrap is a brawl
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A quarrel involving the royal court's fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the jocular definition: a bad violinist scrapes the bow across the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraper is a humorous, slightly scornful name for a fiddle player who saws away at the strings.

clue.text: Novel spectacles include hard seat backed by associate of Cadbury

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take on a new order
backed means put into reverse, so this word runs from back to front
to include is to take something in, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: specs is the informal word for glasses
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a pew is a church bench

explanation.surface: New glasses come with a hard chair, plus a partner of the chocolate firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged glasses split after SC to hold the hard seat, whose bench part is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The drinks maker merged with the chocolate maker in 1969 to form Cadbury Schweppes, so they were corporate partners.

clue.text: Pieces of bull, perhaps

definitions.note: plural definition for a single name covering four operas

blocks.note: first meaning: a cycle of four of the theme's operas known by one name
second meaning: what goes through a bull's nose, or the arena where it fights

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces of bull' looks like cuts of beef; split it, and 'Pieces' is Wagner's four-opera cycle while 'bull' gives a bull-ring or nose ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Der Ring des Nibelungen is Wagner's cycle of four operas, a set of the preamble's pieces in one name.

clue.text: Zoroastrian river piece

blocks.note: a Parsi is a follower of Zoroaster, chiefly in India
the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A section of a river held sacred by a Zoroastrian.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a Cornish river that reaches the sea at Falmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Wagner's last opera, about the Holy Grail, so it is one of the preamble's pieces.

clue.text: Restore what may have been overeaten heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out
the answer is what these letters might once have been, in another order

blocks.note: taken as written; its middle letter E goes

explanation.surface: Bring back what was eaten to excess, done without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' reads as cruelly, but it removes the middle E of a nine-letter word, leaving eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate a building is to restore it to good condition, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A 2 operator's Nazi catchword

blocks.note: taken as written
2 is FLYING; Ryanair is the flying operator, literally Ryan's air

explanation.surface: A slogan used by a Nazi airline worker.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 operator' means a flying operator, an airline; Ryanair is the Irish budget airline, read as Ryan's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazis used the racial term for their supposed master race constantly in propaganda.

clue.text: Piece to see with bird and smile

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a hen is a female bird
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A show to watch featuring a bird and a cheerful smile.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird fits the theme too: Wagner's hero arrives in a boat drawn by a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is Wagner's opera about the swan knight, one of the preamble's pieces.

clue.text: City channel (English, not English) has broken rest

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the English Channel named in a language other than English: French La Manche
taken as written

explanation.surface: A waterway's name loses its English label and its relaxation is disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English, not English' asks for the English Channel in another language; the French call it La Manche, the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is the large city in north-west England, a straightforward example of a city.

clue.text: City of 10's bird?

blocks.note: first meaning: the capital of Ukraine
second meaning: 10's bird is HEN, and chicken stuffed with garlic butter carries the city's name

explanation.walkthrough: 10-across contains HEN, and a chicken dish named after the Ukrainian capital is a familiar menu item.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian capital lends its name to chicken Kiev, a breaded chicken breast filled with garlic butter.

clue.text: Piece going to Sunderland: is it possible?

indicators.note: a possible version is one of several ways things could be ordered, so these letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A doubtful query about whether a work could travel to Sunderland, a city in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is it' belongs to the letters as well as to the question, so the fodder runs from 'to' through 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan und Isolde is Wagner's opera of doomed love, one of the preamble's pieces.

clue.text: No matter that a fiend gets gold — so much is bilingual

blocks.note: un is French for a
an imp is a little devil
or is French and heraldic for gold
tant is French for so much

explanation.surface: It hardly matters that a devil acquires gold, and so much speaks two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is bilingual' warns that some of the pieces are French: 'a', 'gold' and 'so much' all switch language, while the fiend stays English.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no matter, as in 'it's no matter', is trivial and insignificant.

clue.text: I held up joiners to the devil's work force?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
'and' joins words, so joiners are ands

explanation.surface: Someone delayed the carpenters on their way to a hellish job.
explanation.walkthrough: Joiners look like carpenters but are conjunctions. The proverb is 'the devil finds work for idle hands', so they are his labour force.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the devil makes work for the unoccupied, so the lazy are his workforce.

clue.text: Sailor with blemishes doesn't indulge

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
stains are marks or blemishes

explanation.surface: A spotty seaman stays away from life's pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the standard abbreviation for able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from drink or other pleasures declines to indulge, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 2
Complaint that one could hear Forsyth greeting relative?

indicators.note: what one hears is the spoken version, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Bruce Forsyth, a sister and a dropped-h hello run together

explanation.surface: A grumble about a TV host saying hello to a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce Forsyth was a long-running British TV game-show host; say his first name, a cockney ''ello' and 'sis' in one breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Brucellosis is a bacterial disease caught from cattle, and a complaint is an illness.

clue.text: See 13
Piece of a thousand flowers in a department

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
asters are daisy-like garden flowers
taken as written
the Gers is a French département in Gascony

explanation.surface: A section of an office department holding a thousand flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: A department here is one of France's administrative regions, not an office section.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mastersingers of Nuremberg is the English title of Wagner's comic opera Die Meistersinger, one of the preamble's pieces.

clue.text: Franciscan food?

definitions.note: a proper name for one particular friar

blocks.note: first meaning: the name of the jolly friar in Robin Hood's band of outlaws
second meaning: British schoolchildren's slang for snacks and sweets

explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the jolly monk of the Robin Hood legends; tuck is old British school slang for food, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary friar bears the name, and British boarding-school slang uses it for snacks and treats.

clue.text: There's heavenly vision, we hear, with saline solution

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: in heaven, the departed are the ones who behold it

explanation.surface: A mystical vision accompanies a medical salt-water mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavenly vision is what the departed see, and 'see' and 'sea' sound alike. 'Saline solution' sounds clinical but means very salty water.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked lake between Israel and Jordan is one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.

clue.text: Fancy mother entertaining king of Italy!

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
re is Italian for king

explanation.surface: Imagine a mother hosting the Italian monarch!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an exclamation of surprise, but it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an imagined notion or flight of the imagination, a synonym for a dream.

clue.text: Even a king may come up out of a bender

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Even royalty may climb out of a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is slang for a drinking spree, but here it is literally something that bends. E'en is the poetic form of even.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint that lets the leg flex, so it is a thing that bends.

clue.text: Setter's got his love removed from once threatening state

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so a letter is dropped from the following word

blocks.note: the setter says I'm, I am
the setter's property is, in his own words, mine
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written, losing its O

explanation.surface: The setter has had his beloved taken from a formerly menacing nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks of himself, so 'Setter's' is I'm and 'his' is mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminence is the condition of being about to happen, typically of danger looming close.

clue.text: In the dark until switched

indicators.note: switched means swapped around, so these letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sitting in darkness until a light is switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched' fits the surface as a light switch, but it shuffles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that is not illuminated leaves those inside without light, sitting in darkness.

clue.text: See 20
Have you heard "Have some Madeira, ___" after a term and a half?

definitions.text: after a term and a half

indicators.note: asking whether you have heard something points to its spoken sound

blocks.note: the missing words of the song title are a clipped 'my dear'

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone knows the old comic song, sung halfway through the academic year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have Some Madeira, M'Dear' is a comic song by the British duo Flanders and Swann. A school year has three terms, so one and a half terms is its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: With three terms in a British school year, a term and a half in reaches the halfway point.
